findingDetails.title: Auto review cli-opencode dispatch still requires a removed linked worktree
findingDetails.evidence: The cli-opencode branch throws when gitDir equals git-common-dir, then requires a primary main/master worktree and a clean primary checkout. The current fanout runner intentionally uses the current checkout plus unique artifact directories and contains no worktree lifecycle; ADR-007 says the mechanism was removed.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The workflow guard and current runner dispatch path were read together; the current runner's worktree search contains no lifecycle creation or handoff, while the auto YAML guard is unconditional for this executor branch.
findingDetails.recommendation: Remove the stale linked-worktree and clean-primary preflight from the current auto caller, or route it through the current preserve-and-contain contract and add a caller-level test.
findingDetails.claim: A supported cli-opencode deep-review auto run from the current checkout is rejected before executor dispatch because the caller still requires the removed linked-worktree topology.
counterevidenceSought: outer runner always supplies a linked worktree
current fanout runner creates or passes an isolated worktree before this branch
caller test exercises the current no-worktree topology
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: A manually pre-created linked worktree can satisfy the guard, but that is not the current default runner topology and does not reconcile the removed mechanism.

findingDetails.title: Canonical packet requirements still describe removed worktree behavior
findingDetails.evidence: The executive summary, scope, REQ-005/REQ-007, and SC-003/SC-005/SC-006 retain worktree creation, publication, isolation, and checkout-watch behavior as shipped or required. ADR-007 explicitly accepts removal of worktrees, the cone, and their phases.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The packet summary/scope/requirements/success criteria were compared with ADR-007 and the current runner comments and code that identify unique artifact directories, not worktrees.
findingDetails.recommendation: Rewrite or supersede the remaining worktree requirements and success criteria in the canonical packet, then align status and phase-map metadata with the ADR-007 shipped contract.
findingDetails.claim: The packet's canonical normative surface remains internally contradictory: ADR-007 removes worktrees, while summary, scope, requirements, and success criteria still require them.
counterevidenceSought: explicit packet-wide supersession of all worktree rows
current implementation satisfying the retained isolation criteria
a later decision that reinstates worktrees
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: REQ-005 and REQ-007 carry superseded labels, but their retained normative bodies and success criteria still present the removed behavior as part of the packet contract.

findingDetails.title: Acceptance evidence marks removed behavior as met and cites absent or mismatched tests
findingDetails.evidence: AC-012 through AC-018 remain Met even though several require removed worktree behavior; AC-015 cites the absent worktree-lifecycle.vitest.ts, while cited fanout-run lines now cover metadata refresh or index-lock behavior. The packet status and closure/signoff text also conflict.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Acceptance rows, closure text, current test file inventory, and the cited current fanout-run line ranges were compared; the named lifecycle test is absent and the current runner suite has no corresponding lifecycle block.
findingDetails.recommendation: Mark removed worktree criteria superseded with ADR-007, replace stale verification citations with current evidence, and reconcile In Progress/Complete/Closeable/signoff metadata before relying on the packet as a closure gate.
findingDetails.claim: The acceptance artifact overstates completion by treating removed worktree behavior and unsupported citations as met evidence, so it cannot currently serve as a reliable closure gate.
counterevidenceSought: the named worktree-lifecycle test exists at the cited path
current fanout-run lines assert the claimed worktree behavior
all closure/signoff fields agree on the delivered state
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Some rows are explicitly superseded, but the remaining Met rows, absent test citation, and contradictory closure metadata still leave unsupported completion claims.

findingDetails.title: Plan churn thresholds disagree with the shipped defaults
findingDetails.evidence: The plan describes churn above twelve in one window or forty cumulative, while the current executor config and packet requirement use three newly dirty paths and twelve cumulative. The runner consumes the parsed config thresholds.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The plan, requirement, config parser, and runner threshold plumbing were compared in the same pass.
findingDetails.recommendation: Update the plan's threshold rationale to the shipped 3/12 values or record a deliberate versioned change; do not leave conflicting tuning guidance in the canonical packet.
findingDetails.claim: A maintainer following the plan would configure materially different churn thresholds from the ones the shipped runner uses.
counterevidenceSought: later config override that makes 12/40 the effective defaults
a superseding plan section with the 3/12 values
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: This is documentation drift rather than a runtime defect because the parser and requirement currently agree on 3/12.
